record.title: Production EAS Update channel can replace phone JS without an in-repo git digest gate
record.description: TestFlight/production binaries load JS from the Expo updates URL for project dfb4d2a5-1b94-449c-bc28-43466a46803d on channel production, with checkAutomatically ON_LOAD and runtimeVersion 1.1.0. The repo has no GitHub Actions to build, attest, or promote that payload from a git SHA. Anyone who can run eas update --channel production against that project can change field-app behavior independently of git. Expo collaborator lists and token holders were not observed and must not be probed.
record.claimed_root_cause: The phone updater is bound to a mutable EAS channel name and Expo project URL, not to an in-repo immutable digest or CI promotion workflow.

trace.description: EAS production profile publishes to channel production.
Enabled updates.url points at u.expo.dev for this project, checkAutomatically ON_LOAD, fallbackToCacheTimeout 0.
Installed 1.1.0 binaries accept any update Expo serves for that runtime and production channel, with no in-repo workflow binding the bundle to a git commit.

evidence.description: updates.checkAutomatically is ON_LOAD so a published channel payload is applied at app start.
Production EAS build.env pins EXPO_PUBLIC_API_BASE to the Railway API; eas update is a separate publish path that does not require this repo's CI.
Server updates are git-push rebuilds; mobile OTA is not described as a digest-pinned promotion in that deploy path, and no .github workflows exist in scope.

record.reason: Cited lines are real at c661a8fd (eas.json production.channel, app.json updates.url/ON_LOAD/runtimeVersion 1.1.0, DEPLOY.md git-push for the API/web, no .github workflows). Publish still requires Expo login as owner vtz1900 or that account's EXPO_TOKEN (mobile/README.md; mobile/app.json owner/extra.eas.projectId). No lower-trust principal (anonymous client, staff JWT, GitHub PR, unauthenticated HTTP) can ship a production-channel payload without already holding those Expo credentials, and there is no in-repo CI a contributor could trigger as a confused deputy. eas update by the Expo project principal is the documented same-principal OTA path. Binding the channel to a git digest is a release-control/hygiene gap, not a cross-boundary result. An unobserved Expo collaborator list does not name a lower-trust actor: any such person would already hold Expo credentials. The first trace step is operator profile config, not a lower-trust entrypoint.
